IV access 18–20g in the arm OPPOSITE the symptomatic side. Arterial, and venous at radiologist discretion.

Rad to confirm whether a 2nd acquisition with the arm down (both phases, same coverage) is needed.

customScanGuide.Neck Soft Tissue CT W/ Contrast|with|non:
Coverage -  Skull base to the top of the aortic-arch.
Patient preparation
Remove metal related to the neck area (necklaces, undergarments).
Instruct the patient to be steady and not to swallow during the procedure.
Ask to breath slowly during the procedure.
Assess the ability to administer contrast media and expose radiation.
Place a cannula in a stable vein for contrast injection – pink-20G cannula.
Patient positioning
Position in head-first and supine.
Extend the neck slightly.
Explanation: reduces streak artifacts or beam hardening artifacts due to the lower jaw. Same results can be achieved by angulating CT gantry.
Position the shoulders in a pulled down position and arms next to the body.
Explanation: reduces streak artifacts or beam hardening artifacts due to wide shoulders. Placing a cushion under mid-upper thorax moves shoulders posteriorly, and helps to reduce streak artifacts at the root of the neck

customScanGuide.Cardiac Coronary CTA|with|none|cardiac|7:
ECG-gated coronary CTA (cardiac pulse, <65 bpm target):
No caffeine or exercise 12 hrs prior. No ED meds (sildenafil etc.) 4 days prior.
Nitroglycerine sublingual may be given per site protocol for coronary dilation.
4-lead ECG placement: 2 mid-clavicular + 2 lateral rib cage 5" from midline. Supine, feet first.
Includes a calcium-score pre-scan, then SmartPrep bolus tracking — ROI on the descending aorta — then the gated pulse acquisition.
IV contrast volume and rate per P3T, with a mixed contrast/saline bolus.
See Series & Reconstructions for the full acquisition chain — final scoring/recon is done in TeraRecon per the cardiac reference book.
